To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. we have collected and organized a public dataset of blood images for the evaluation of image analysis algorithms; 2. we have defined a set of figures of merit to compare the results of the different algorithms; 3. we have proposed a method to segment blood samples and detect leukemia cells; 4. we have compared the results of our segmentation method against the state of the art algorithms.
the proposed dataset is a new and unique tool for the comparison of algorithms in the field of image processing for the analysis of blood samples.
we propose a new dataset of images of blood samples, with a specific classification of the cells and a set of figures of merit to evaluate the performance of the algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects:

the following questions: How can we build a dataset of blood cells for leukemia diagnosis? How can we evaluate and compare the performance of different algorithms? What is the best way to share the data and the results?
the development of new algorithms for the analysis of images of blood samples, and the design of a new database for the evaluation of such algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the All-IDB dataset is an important contribution to the field of leukemia diagnosis and it is a useful tool to compare different algorithms in the field of image processing.

the dataset is a useful tool to evaluate the performances of algorithms for segmentation, classification and counting of blood samples, and it is freely available to the scientific community for the development and testing of new methods.
the dataset presented here, is a valuable resource for the development and testing of new methods for the analysis of blood samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an online repository of images of peripheral blood samples for the diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemias, with the aim of offering a new tool to researchers in the image processing field.
the dataset is composed of a set of 200 images, each one with 100 cells to be segmented and classified.
the dataset is available at http://www.dibris.unige.it/all-idb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the availability of such datasets is crucial to foster the research in the field and to promote the development of new and more accurate tools.
the proposed database is an open source and publicly accessible resource, and it can be used by researchers and practitioners to evaluate and compare their algorithms.
the proposed dataset can be used to test the performance of different segmentation and classification algorithms, as well as to compare different approaches to the analysis of blood cells.
